label: February 23–March 01
title: “Is Any Thing Too Hard for the Lord” —  Genesis 18

items.text: Abraham and Sarah’s life, filled with events both heartbreaking and heartwarming, is evidence of a truth Abraham learned in a vision—that we are on earth to be proven, “to see if [we] will do all things whatsoever the Lord [our] God shall command.” Would they prove faithful?
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Abraham and Sarah trusted God, and He trusted them. In Genesis 18–23, we find stories that can prompt us to think about our own willingness to believe God’s promises, to flee wickedness and never look back, and to trust God regardless of the sacrifice.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: In proving us, God also improves us. The Lord has made glorious promises to the faithful, but sometimes circumstances can cause us to wonder how these promises can possibly be fulfilled. Abraham and Sarah may have felt that way.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Lord fulfills His promises in His own time. What do you learn from Abraham and Sarah’s experiences about sustaining faith when promised blessings are not received in this life? How can you sustain your faith?
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Lord commands me to flee wickedness and not look back. As we read about Lot and his family, consider how the Lord helps you and your family find protection from evil influences. Are you looking forward with faith in the Savior?
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: “Apparently, what was wrong with Lot’s wife was that she wasn’t just _looking_ back; in her heart she wanted to _go_ back. … Her attachment to the past outweighed her confidence in the future.”

“Faith is for the future. Faith builds on the past but never longs to stay there. Faith trusts that God has great things in store for each of us and that Christ truly is the ‘high priest of good things to come.’”

Dwelling on past lives, including past mistakes, is just not right! It is not the gospel of Jesus Christ. I plead with you not to dwell on days now gone nor to yearn vainly for yesterdays, however good those yesterdays may have been.

Abraham’s willingness to sacrifice Isaac is a similitude of God and His Son. Although we don’t know all the reasons God commanded Abraham to offer Isaac as a sacrifice, we do know it was a test of his faith in God.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Abraham learned in a vision that we are on earth to be proven, “to see if [we] will do all things whatsoever the Lord [our] God shall command.” This testing is designed not only to prove our faithfulness but also to improve us.
